alignments.note: The ASV recasts the bare participial phrase as a concessive clause; the discontinuous frame “Though it be … yet”, including its supplied dummy subject and copula, is a helper on the conjunction that licenses the recasting under rules 7 and 15, as ἀλλά takes “But this cometh to pass” at JHN.15.25 and μήποτε takes “Can it be that” at JHN.7.26. Rule 63 forbids putting the copula on the predicate nominal “covenant”, the English predicate being a noun phrase. The head is “yet”, ὅμως's lexical anchor (JHN.12.42). A narrower “Though … yet” with “it be” read as added remains defensible.
The ASV expands “a man's” with the limiting “but” (cf. REV.12.12 “but a short”).

review_notes: The accepted alignment is retained except in the supplied concessive frame: all 12 source IDs and all 29 target IDs are partitioned exactly once.

The whole supplied frame “Though it be … yet” rides on ὅμως, which licenses the recasting; rule 63 keeps the supplied copula off the predicate nominal “covenant”, so διαθήκην is an ordinary noun alignment.
The resultative rendering “maketh it void” is correctly headed on “void,” and the participial clause is correctly headed on “confirmed.”
